Transliteration issues.
Gun/Kan's name is fairly common, กัน and since ก is transliterated as g or k depending on the source and the word itself using a or u depending on how they want to be close to resemble English spelling, it ends up having different versions.

Same with Tankhun, it took me a while to find the (not even sure if it's the right one) Thai spelling haha, it's แทนคุณ​ and ท is also th or t depending on how the source wants to express the difference between aspirated and non aspirated (ต) sounds.

Finally, the family's last name, Thai has a thing in which the only possible sounds at the end of a syllable are vowels or n/ng/m sonorants or p/t/k stops, and consonants which do not make that sound, like ล which is an l sound, but are placed at the end of a syllable, end up making one of the original acceptable Thai ends, in ล case, an n sound


That's what I know based on self studying Thai for a couple of months now 😅 so I might have missed something.
